PagerBot: INCIDENT P-2026-0423 detected in embeddings-serving (us-west-2) · 03:42 UTC · auto-assigned to Diego R · https://pager.redwood.internal/incidents/P-2026-0423
Asha K: quick handoff note — small but noisy 503 spike for embeddings that started at ~03:42 and resolved by 03:49 after failover and cache leader stabilization. saw a 7m window with 5–10% higher 503s for batch-heavy customers. no ongoing customer pages as of now.
Diego R: confirmed — I handled the mitigation. TL;DR: root cause looked like coordinated eviction on kv-cache leader under memory pressure after a config change to eviction.window. that caused leader transfer thrash and a momentary inability to serve hot prefixes.
Mina S: thanks — can you list the exact steps you ran so I can reproduce in runbook?
Diego R: steps below, copying into the thread for runbook updates.
Diego R: ran health check and scaled cache pool + rolled back eviction.window change. commands:
```
# quick checks
kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=kv-cache -o wide
kubectl -n infra exec svc/kv-cache -- sh -c 'ps aux | grep kv-cache'
# scale up replicas temporarily
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/kv-cache --replicas=6
# rollback config
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/kv-cache EVICTION_WINDOW=old_value
# verify leader stability
kubectl -n infra logs deployment/kv-cache | tail -n 200 | grep leader | tail
```
Asha K: verified downstream routing fell back to read replicas during leader shuffle; I toggled routing weight to reduce blast radius while Diego scaled.
Mina S: noted that the US-WEST incident briefly impacted a single large customer job; CS pinged with one transient failure, they retried and job completed. no SLA violation reported so far.
Diego R: added the alert IDs we hit: alerts/kv-cache-leader-flap (fired 12 times), alerts/503-rate (fired 3 times). I muted noisy duplicates after confirming suppression scope.
Asha K: CURRENT STATUS: embeddings-serving stable in us-west-2, leader flaps stopped, replica count at 6, eviction.window rolled back. small amount of error telemetry retained for postmortem.
Mina S: COVERAGE & HANDOFF: I'm taking primary for the next 6h window (04:00–10:00 UTC) to watch APAC cold start patterns, Diego will be secondary for 4h (04:00–08:00) then off. @Diego R pls ack if that matches your plan.
Diego R: ack. I'll remain reachable for 04:00–08:00 for escalation.
Asha K: RUNBOOK / LINKS: please add the exact command snippet above to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-leader-flap (small edit: include scale and rollback steps). High-level postmortem checklist: 1) timeline + root cause 2) config rollout guardrails 3) alert tuning to reduce dup noise 4) customer comms check.
Mina S: I'll schedule a quick 30m blameless review tomorrow 09:30 UTC and create PM with action items.
SRE Bot: follow-up task created — RED-OPS-2026-88 "kv-cache eviction regression follow-up" assigned to Asha K and Mina S · https://tasks.redwood.internal/RED-OPS-2026-88
Asha K: NEXT STEPS (short):
- Asha: update runbook with the commands + diagnostics (ETA 2h)
- Mina: create postmortem draft and schedule review (ETA 24h)
- Diego: add note to recent config rollout PR about observed behavior (ETA next PR update)
- Ops: monitor for repeated flaps and keep alerts unmuted after review
Diego R: one very small follow-up: we should consider adding a soft-threshold alert that triggers before leader transfer count spikes (will propose thresholds).
Mina S: noted. coverage gap check — we have no night APAC primary for 22:00–02:00 UTC later this week; I'll follow up with rotation leads to fill that slot.
Asha K: closing thread — if any page hits again, reopen P-2026-0423 and ping on this thread. thanks team :thumbsup:
